mods.name: BuildShapes
mods.description:
Draw curves, mirror building groups, and repeat decorations along a curve as shared BuildOrders ghosts. Requires BuildOrders with its planning and ghost-selection APIs.

With a hammer and building piece selected, close the piece menu. F4 opens Curve; Shift+F4 opens Mirror; Ctrl+F4 opens Repeat. F4 or Escape exits any mode. Shift+click marks points, L submits, U removes your last shape's unbuilt ghosts, and Backspace removes the last marker. Exit with F4 to build normally with E.

Curve: select a beam/pole and mark start, bend, end. Native-length beams follow the curve in 3D with overlapping joints. Requires two endpoint snap points and a span of 0.25–8 metres.

Mirror: mark two points for a vertical mirror plane, then Ctrl+click built pieces or visible ghosts to toggle source selection. Thin wire boxes show sources; heavier boxes preview copies. Ctrl+Backspace removes the last selection. Reflection axes and pivot compensation follow native snap layouts, fixing triangular under-roof walls and sloped beams while preserving ordinary roof pitch; mesh bounds are a fallback. Asymmetric carvings and handed meshes keep their original geometry, so inspect the ghosts before building.

Repeat: mark start, bend, end with any normal building piece selected. An options panel opens automatically beside the preview: choose a Path anchor (piece origin, visual center, or a native snap point), spacing, yaw, pitch, roll, and whether to turn with the curve. Changes preview live. For precise adjustments, type a value then Enter/Apply, or use ± buttons (0.05 m / 1°; Shift: 0.01 m / 0.1°). Sliders keep exact values until dragged. Confirm applies pending numeric entries and submits, Edit path replaces the end, and Cancel exits. Escape closes options without losing the path; L reopens. Slider clicks never mark the world or attack. Spacing fits evenly to both endpoints; the chosen anchor stays on the path after rotation, marked by gold crosses. Choose Bottom for a post base or an end snap for a beam. There is no automatic terrain alignment. Curve-following preserves the seed's initial heading/tilt, then applies rotation offsets. Outside the panel, Ctrl+click copies a built piece/ghost and its orientation; [ / ], Page Up/Down, and Home remain available.

Preview strokes/boxes are local and approximate; L creates full shared planner ghosts. Curves are limited to 128 metres and all tools to 256 pieces. Markers/sources require 40-metre reach; the planner checks all output positions, recipes, wards, and no-build areas. Scaled and terrain-operation pieces are excluded. Selections are pose snapshots.

Terrain and built pieces stay intact; normal materials/support still apply. Undo is one submitted shape across all tools and clears on death, world change, or F6. Only the designer needs BuildShapes; participating players should use updated BuildOrders and the selected pieces. Ghost selection, mirror mesh alignment, multiplayer, and fresh-launch behavior need gameplay testing.
mods.notes: 0.2.3: Repeat now offers exact numeric entry and fine ± buttons for spacing and all rotation axes. Hold Shift for 0.01 m / 0.1° steps. Enter/Apply updates the preview; Confirm validates and applies pending edits. Sliders preserve precise values until dragged, and scrollable options keep the action buttons visible.

mods.name: Farmhand
mods.description:
Plant spaced rows and harvest/replant nearby crops with your cultivator. See why unhealthy plants cannot grow.

Equip a cultivator and select a crop. Hold Left Shift to preview a row, and press J to plant it. Hold Left Shift and press U to harvest nearby mature crops and replant the same types; also hold Left Ctrl to harvest without replanting.

Every planted crop uses normal seeds/materials, stamina, and cultivator durability. Normal placement reach, cultivated soil, biome, sunlight, spacing, and protected areas still apply. Harvested drops remain normal world items; bring seeds before replanting. BuildFromChests can supply seeds while the cultivator is equipped.

Supports crop and seed-crop pieces in the cultivator, not trees, vines, wild berries, or respawning plants. New controls and batch sizes are configurable through the mod manager. Turn off BuildOrders plan mode before using batch actions. Peers and the host do not need Farmhand.
mods.notes: 0.1.1: Default controls use Left Shift instead of Right Alt. Left Ctrl is the configurable harvest-only modifier, so Shift + U still replants.

mods.name: Gary
mods.description:
Gary the Greydwarf is a purple forest companion: friendly, defensive, impossible to kill, and occasionally generous with snacks. Uses the game's native Greydwarf body, movement, weapons, and animation; no API key or external service required.

F3 summons one Gary per player, or recalls that same Gary beside you. Shift+F3 tells him to stay where he is; F3 resumes following. Both keys are configurable. Calls need clear dry ground nearby. He waits outside dungeons and for you to respawn; use F3 to call him after a portal trip.

Gary follows quietly until a hostile creature actually damages his player or Gary himself. He defends against that attacker for up to 30 seconds and stays within a bounded defense radius. He can defend himself while waiting, including outside a dungeon or while his player is dead/offline, and resumes waiting afterward. He does not pick fights with nearby wildlife, players, or tamed friends. Friendly player/pet hits do not hurt him.

At 20% health, Gary abandons combat and tries to flee 40 metres from you. Damage cannot take his health below 5%, and native death checks are suppressed for Gary alone. He heals rapidly at a safe distance, slowly while escaping, and comes back at 90%. If his zone unloads, a saved three-minute recovery deadline lets him heal before being recalled. Calling him does not interrupt his retreat.

Outside combat, he occasionally tosses one free raspberry, blueberry, or mushroom near your feet (roughly every 3–5 minutes by default). Gifts land as normal items on the ground; the cooldown persists across F6 and world saves.

Within 90 metres, Gary can notice a loaded burial chamber, sunken crypt, troll cave, or frost cave entrance. He leads a little way ahead, waits if you lag behind, and gives up if the route is obstructed. He remembers the last 32 entrances he showed you. He cannot tell whether a dungeon is cleared, does not reveal distant locations or map pins, and waits outside rather than entering.

Install Gary on the host/dedicated server and participating clients for multiplayer. The server authenticates commands and finds the existing saved Gary, including unloaded zones, before spawning. Creature simulation and gifts run only on its network owner. Uses tagged vanilla Greydwarf saves, so removing the mod leaves a normal tamed greydwarf instead of an unknown-prefab object. Special behavior and purple appearance require the mod.

Settings are in F7 → Mod settings, or BepInEx/config/com.bobisme.gary.cfg. First release: compiled and checked against native Linux game assemblies, with injury/defense/gift/guide policy tests. Appearance, pathfinding, tossing, multiplayer, and save/restart behavior need an in-game playtest.
mods.notes: 0.1.2: Fixed Gary ignoring creatures that attacked him without attacking his player. Remembers verified attackers for bounded self-defense, including while waiting. Stops chasing dead, friendly, stale, or distant attackers; healing retreats still take priority.

mods.name: PolygonLeveler
mods.description:
Mark a convex polygon with your hoe, level it horizontally, or flatten it into a smooth sloped plane.

Hold a hoe. Left Shift + left click places a marker. L levels it to the first marker's height. Shift + L fits the closest plane to the current ground, removing bumps while keeping the average slope; the outline updates to that plane. U undoes the last polygon. Backspace removes the last marker and Delete clears the outline. All keys are configurable.

Uses normal terrain saving and network ownership, checks wards and the game's height limits, preserves ground paint, and edits only terrain-grid vertices inside the convex boundary. The visible edge follows the terrain's triangles. Costs one hoe use per polygon, with no stone cost.

Undo restores original heights and smoothing without refunding the hoe use. It refuses conflicting edits and checks current ward permissions and distance. Undo history lasts ten minutes, clears on reload, and requires the original terrain owner to remain available. An interrupted undo can be retried. Only leveling done with this version can be undone.

The fitted plane minimizes squared vertical height changes over the selected ground vertices, counting tile seams once. Polygons too narrow to define a plane are rejected. Install 0.1.3 or newer on the host and participating players for Shift + L in multiplayer. Markers are local previews and disappear on reload. Changes to the ground persist normally. Gameplay and multiplayer still need an in-game playtest.
mods.notes: 0.1.3: Shift + L flattens the current ground to a least-squares fitted plane, preserving its average slope. L still levels horizontally to the first marker. Tile seams count once in the fit, the outline shows the fitted plane, normal terrain limits are checked for every target height, and U undoes either action. Multiplayer owners need 0.1.3 for fitted planes.
